response.basis: Contract extraction from NL1-NL10 describing a train door/motion state machine: DoorsClosing -> InMotion -> {Stopping, EmergencyStopping}; InMotion substates Accelerating -> Cruising -> Approaching with entry/exit actions and signals.

binding_hints.reason: The root scope owns the required initial edge.
DoorsClosing is the state entered by the initial edge.

contracts.normative_statement: The root system must have an initial entry edge into the DoorsClosing state.
contracts.quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state
contracts.reason: NL explicitly states the system starts in DoorsClosing, establishing a required initial pseudostate edge.

binding_hints.reason: DoorsClosing is the explicit origin of the transition.
InMotion is the explicit destination.
The named signal causes this exact transition.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorsClosing must have a transition to InMotion triggered by the Closed/SendDeparted signal.
contracts.quote: transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal
contracts.reason: NL explicitly states the exact transition endpoint pair from DoorsClosing to InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the explicit shared origin.
Stopping is the destination of this alternative.
The named signal indicates arrival causing this transition.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have a transition to Stopping triggered by the Arrived signal.
contracts.quote: transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal
contracts.reason: NL explicitly establishes an endpoint from InMotion to Stopping distinct from the EmergencyStopping alternative.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the explicit shared origin.
EmergencyStopping is the destination of this alternative.
This is a data condition rather than a named signal, distinguishing it as a guard.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have a transition to EmergencyStopping guarded by obstacle detection.
contracts.quote: or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
contracts.reason: NL explicitly establishes an alternate endpoint from InMotion to EmergencyStopping conditioned on obstacle detection.

binding_hints.reason: Shared source of the two alternatives requiring disjointness.
First alternative target.
Second alternative target.

contracts.normative_statement: The Stopping and EmergencyStopping alternatives from InMotion must be distinguishable and mutually exclusive.
contracts.quote: the system can either transition to the Stopping state ... or to the EmergencyStopping state
contracts.reason: The either/or phrasing establishes an explicit mutual-exclusion requirement between the two alternatives.

binding_hints.reason: The state that must perform the action.
The exact required action.

contracts.normative_statement: The EmergencyStopping state must perform the Emergency Stop action.
contracts.quote: which includes the actions "Emergency Stop"
contracts.reason: NL explicitly requires the Emergency Stop action to occur in EmergencyStopping, but no exact lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit) is stated.

binding_hints.reason: The state that must perform the action.
The exact required signaling action.
Names the signal sent by this action.

contracts.normative_statement: The EmergencyStopping state must send the Obstacle Detected signal.
contracts.quote: and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal
contracts.reason: NL explicitly requires sending the Obstacle Detected signal as a distinct action from Emergency Stop.

binding_hints.reason: The composite owning the substate.
The contained child state.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain Accelerating as a child state.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL explicitly places Accelerating as a substate within InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: The composite owning the substate.
The contained child state.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain Cruising as a child state.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL explicitly places Cruising as a substate within InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: The composite owning the substate.
The contained child state.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain Approaching as a child state.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL explicitly places Approaching as a substate within InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: The composite scope carrying the cardinality obligation.
The explicit finite named member set.

cardinality_requirement.reason: NL names exactly three substates explicitly; this is also consistent with a direct_child_states count since no other children are mentioned.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have exactly three direct child substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching.
contracts.quote: the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL explicitly counts three named direct child substates of InMotion, an explicit finite named list.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the enclosing composite owning the initial substate edge.
Accelerating is the substate entered by the initial edge.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have an initial entry edge into the Accelerating substate.
contracts.quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate
contracts.reason: Discourse establishes InMotion as the enclosing owner from NL4; this clause states the owner-local first substate entry.

binding_hints.reason: Accelerating is the explicit origin.
Cruising is the explicit destination.
Named signal causing the transition.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must have a transition to Cruising triggered by the Reached Cruising signal.
contracts.quote: moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal
contracts.reason: NL explicitly establishes the endpoint pair and triggering signal.

binding_hints.reason: Accelerating is the explicit origin per this segment.
Approaching is the explicit destination.
Named signal causing the transition.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must have a transition to Approaching triggered by the Approached/Decelerate signal when approaching the destination.
contracts.quote: it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal
contracts.reason: NL explicitly establishes this endpoint pair distinct from the Accelerating-to-Cruising endpoint.

binding_hints.reason: Cruising is the explicit origin.
Approaching is the explicit destination.
Named signal causing the transition.

contracts.normative_statement: Cruising must have a transition to Approaching triggered by the Approached/Decelerate signal.
contracts.quote: The system in the Cruising substate transitions to the Approaching substate when it approaches the destination, triggered by the "Approached/Decelerate" signal
contracts.reason: NL explicitly establishes this endpoint pair as a distinct relation from the Accelerating-to-Approaching relation.

binding_hints.reason: The state whose entry action is required.
Entry/Accelerate explicitly names the entry lifecycle phase.
The exact required action on entry.

contracts.normative_statement: The Accelerating state must perform the Accelerate action on entry.
contracts.quote: marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action
contracts.reason: NL explicitly supplies state, exact lifecycle phase entry, and exact action Accelerate, satisfying the full S4 triple.

binding_hints.reason: The state performing the continuous action.
The exact continuous activity required in this state.
binding_hints.value: send Send signal and continue approaching

binding_hints.reason: Names the signal sent as part of this continuous action.

contracts.normative_statement: The Approaching state must continuously send the Send signal while approaching the destination.
contracts.quote: the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination
contracts.reason: NL explicitly requires a continuous/ongoing activity (sending Send signal and continuing to approach) distinct from a mere mention, warranting an independent state_action obligation.

binding_hints.reason: The state whose retention is required.
The condition bounding the retention obligation.
binding_hints.value: until ready to stop or decelerate

contracts.normative_statement: The system must retain the Approaching substate until it is ready to stop or decelerate.
contracts.quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate
contracts.reason: NL explicitly establishes a retention obligation for Approaching bounded by an eventual stop/decelerate condition; no scenario or interval is invented here.

cardinality_bindings.basis: NL4 text: 'Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'; exact_source_inventory.states (InMotion at line 5); inspection_equivalent_facts.states (state:InMotion:line:13); NL-CONTRACT-NL4-CARD-1 binding_hints owner=InMotion domain=Accelerating,Cruising,Approaching.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 directly counts three named substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) that the discourse explicitly places within/owned by InMotion ('Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates'). This is a direct child-state count, not a region/partition claim: no parallel/orthogonal/concurrent language is present. The owner concept InMotion maps exactly to the closed-model state ref state:InMotion:line:13 (inspection_equivalent_facts.states). Although the closed model does not structurally nest these three states under InMotion as parent (see the containment candidates), the cardinality contract's owner/scope binding is still exact because InMotion is uniquely identified and is the only candidate scope for this obligation; the counting-domain reading itself is not ambiguous even though the structural containment fact independently fails.

response.reason: This lens compared each supplied NL contract's exact typed obligation against the exact closed FCSTM transition/state inventory, the exact author-source inventory (PlantUML lines), and the working-contract source-to-model mapping. Endpoint contracts (NL1, NL2x2, NL5, NL6, NL7) all resolve to exact matching FCSTM edges with matching triggers/guards where required, so they are omitted. The InMotion->EmergencyStopping vs InMotion->Stopping guard_disjointness contract (NL2-DISJ-1) is flagged because both alternatives are triggered by distinct named events (Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived vs Obstacle_Detected) with no guard predicate encoded anywhere in the closed model or source, so no exact disjointness proof is possible and the qualifier remains unsupported as a formal property (kept W1, predicate null). The cardinality contract for InMotion's three substates is bound to owner InMotion via exact source/model identity match; the closed inventory shows Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching all present as InMotion-targeted states with no separator (single implicit region, direct_child_states domain). The initial_entry contracts (root->DoorsClosing, InMotion-local->Accelerating) are checked against the exact source/model edges: root initial edge to DoorsClosing exists (S2 satisfied, omitted). However, InMotion itself has no exact 'initial'/default pseudostate edge distinguishing Accelerating as its local first-entry target from its three unconditional child edges (InMotion->Accelerating, InMotion->Cruising, InMotion->Approaching all appear as ordinary transitions with no trigger, i.e., structurally indistinguishable default entries), so NL5-INIT-1 remains an unresolved/violated owner-local initial edge distinguishability problem. Containment contracts (NL4-CONTAIN-1/2/3) are structurally satisfied only if InMotion is read as an owning composite, but the exact closed FCSTM inventory models InMotion as a flat sibling state (not a composite parent) that merely has ordinary sibling-like transitions to Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching, not structural containment edges; the model's own composite flag only marks the root wrapper as composite, not InMotion. This exposes a structural containment defect for all three contracts. The termination/state-action/retention/event-consumption contracts already surfaced their own rows in a prior round and are unresolved-independent here except where this lens sees a distinct structural angle (event-consumer coverage was already exact per inspection facts and is omitted).

issues.observed: The closed FCSTM only shows InMotion with three unconditional, untriggered ordinary transitions to Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching (transition:line:32/35/37, all guard=null, triggers=[]), with no pseudostate or default-entry marker distinguishing Accelerating as the required first-entered substate; all three are structurally identical alternatives from InMotion.
issues.reason: NL5 states InMotion must begin specifically in Accelerating, but the closed model's InMotion->Accelerating edge is structurally indistinguishable (no trigger, no guard, no pseudostate marking) from equally-weighted InMotion->Cruising and InMotion->Approaching edges, so there is no exact mechanism enforcing that Accelerating is entered first/by default as the contract requires.

The InMotion->EmergencyStopping vs InMotion->Stopping guard_disjointness contract (NL2-DISJ-1) is flagged because both alternatives are triggered by distinct named events (Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived vs Obstacle_Detected) with no guard predicate encoded anywhere in the closed model or source, so no exact disjointness proof is possible and the qualifier remains unsupported as a formal property (kept W1, predicate null). The cardinality contract for InMotion's three substates is bound to owner InMotion via exact source/model identity match; the closed inventory shows Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching all present as InMotion-targeted states with no separator (single implicit region, direct_child_states domain). The initial_entry contracts (root->DoorsClosing, InMotion-local->Accelerating) are checked against the exact source/model edges: root initial edge to DoorsClosing exists (S2 satisfied, omitted). However, InMotion itself has no exact 'initial'/default pseudostate edge distinguishing Accelerating as its local first-entry target from its three unconditional child edges (InMotion->Accelerating, InMotion->Cruising, InMotion->Approaching all appear as ordinary transitions with no trigger, i.e., structurally indistinguishable default entries), so NL5-INIT-1 remains an unresolved/violated owner-local initial edge distinguishability problem. Containment contracts (NL4-CONTAIN-1/2/3) are structurally satisfied only if InMotion is read as an owning composite, but the exact closed FCSTM inventory models InMotion as a flat sibling state (not a composite parent) that merely has ordinary sibling-like transitions to Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching, not structural containment edges; the model's own composite flag only marks the root wrapper as composite, not InMotion. This exposes a structural containment defect for all three contracts. The termination/state-action/retention/event-consumption contracts already surfaced their own rows in a prior round and are unresolved-independent here except where this lens sees a distinct structural angle (event-consumer coverage was already exact per inspection facts and is omitted).

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, and stable termination. Key findings: (1) EmergencyStopping->[*] (transition:line:31) is triggered by Obstacle_Cleared, not by the Obstacle_Detected event that NL3 requires EmergencyStopping itself to send/consume - the sent Obstacle_Detected event is actually consumed by InMotion (transition:line:30), which is a different scope than the sending state; this satisfies event_consumption in a technical sense since InMotion consumes it, so NL3-DERIVED contract is satisfied and omitted. (2) The Stopping state (final NL termination target per NL2/NL10) is a reachable leaf with NO outgoing transition (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic, verify deadlock check 'refuted') - this is a genuine dead-end/frontier fact requiring a V1 deadlock_freedom-style candidate, but no explicit deadlock_freedom contract exists for Stopping in the supplied contract set. However supplied termination-state role only appears null across contracts (final_states per canonical IR are EmergencyStopping and Approaching, not Stopping) - Stopping is an operating_state per NL2/NL10 endpoint contracts, so its dead-end nature is a behavioral consequence worth flagging via a derived contract since NL clearly expects Stopping to represent a stable resting/final condition (train arrived and stopped) implied by NL2 'transition to the Stopping state when it arrives' and NL10 'until it is ready to stop' -> Stopping is the intended stop destination, and a state representing 'stopped' with zero outgoing transitions and no formal final marking is a dead-end violation of implicit stable-continuation semantics. I derive one state_retention/deadlock-adjacent contract narrowly for this. (3) EmergencyStopping and Approaching both route to [*] as true final states matching canonical source (final_states list) - termination via Obstacle_Cleared and Destination_Missed are well-formed, no re-entry cycle observed, so NL-CONTRACT termination-adjacent facts are satisfied and omitted. (4) Event consumer coverage: Obstacle_Detected declared/reachable consumer is InMotion (transition:line:30) - which is the correct consuming scope for the transition matching NL2-ENDPOINT-2; consumption is fine. Arrived event (line:29) consumed at InMotion - fine. Closed_SendDeparted consumed at DoorsClosing - fine. All declared events have reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts, so REF-019/020/021 (NL3-DERIVED, NL1-DERIVED, NL2-DERIVED) event_consumption contracts are satisfied and omitted from candidates.
